lessonTitle: Anaemia: Classification, Deficiency States, Haemolysis and Haemoglobinopathies

blocks.text: A 41-year-old teacher has felt breathless climbing stairs for months. She has been craving ice, her nails are brittle and her haemoglobin is 84 g/L with a mean cell volume of 69 fL. One number, the MCV, already narrows the causes from dozens to a handful; the rest of the work is finding why.

blocks.markdown: **Anaemia** is a reduction in haemoglobin concentration below the reference range for age and sex (commonly below about 130 g/L in adult men and 120 g/L in adult non-pregnant women; ranges vary by laboratory). Haemoglobin carries oxygen, so symptoms reflect reduced oxygen delivery: fatigue, breathlessness, pallor, palpitations. Anaemia is a sign, never a final diagnosis; the question is always why. The most useful first step is the **mean cell volume (MCV)**, the average size of red cells.

blocks.caption: Mean cell volume from the haematocrit and the red cell count.

rows: Iron deficiency, thalassaemia trait, anaemia of chronic disease (sometimes), sideroblastic anaemia
Acute blood loss, anaemia of chronic disease, chronic kidney disease, haemolysis, marrow failure
Vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, alcohol, hypothyroidism, liver disease, some drugs, myelodysplasia
blocks.caption: Classification of anaemia by red cell size. Cut-offs vary by laboratory.

blocks.title: Calculating and classifying MCV
blocks.prompt: A blood count shows haematocrit 0.28 L/L and red cell count 4.0 x 10^12/L. Calculate the MCV and classify the anaemia.

steps.text: 70 fL is below 80 fL so the cells are microcytic.
Microcytic anaemia leads you to iron studies and a blood film looking for hypochromic, pencil-shaped cells (iron deficiency) or target cells (thalassaemia).

blocks.markdown: **Iron studies and the blood film.** In iron deficiency serum ferritin (the storage protein) is low, total iron-binding capacity (TIBC) is high as the body makes more transferrin, and transferrin saturation is low. In anaemia of chronic disease, inflammation raises hepcidin, which traps iron in stores: ferritin is normal or high, TIBC is low or normal, and iron is low. Thalassaemia trait has normal iron studies, a low MCV out of proportion to mild anaemia and a high red cell count; the **Mentzer index** (MCV divided by red cell count) below about 13 favours thalassaemia over iron deficiency. Ferritin is also an acute phase protein, so inflammation can mask iron deficiency.

blocks.caption: Fraction of transferrin binding sites carrying iron.

blocks.title: Interpreting iron studies
blocks.prompt: A woman has Hb 92 g/L, MCV 68 fL, ferritin 7 micrograms/L, serum iron 4 micromol/L, TIBC 70 micromol/L. Calculate the transferrin saturation and interpret.

steps.text: Low saturation, low ferritin and high TIBC together indicate iron deficiency, not chronic disease.
Next ask where the iron is going: menstrual loss, gastrointestinal loss (in men and postmenopausal women investigate the gut), poor intake or malabsorption such as coeliac disease.

blocks.answer: Transferrin saturation about 5.7%: iron deficiency anaemia needing a source search.

blocks.markdown: **Deficiency states and their treatment.** *Iron deficiency* is treated by finding and correcting the cause and replacing iron, usually with oral ferrous salts (for example ferrous sulfate 200 mg once daily or on alternate days, as a teaching example), with intravenous iron if oral therapy is not tolerated or absorbed. *Vitamin B12 deficiency* arises from pernicious anaemia (autoimmune loss of intrinsic factor, with anti-intrinsic factor antibodies), gastric or ileal disease or a strict vegan diet. It causes macrocytosis with hypersegmented neutrophils and, importantly, neurological damage (subacute combined degeneration of the cord, neuropathy). Treatment is intramuscular hydroxocobalamin. *Folate deficiency* arises from poor intake, alcohol, pregnancy, haemolysis, malabsorption and methotrexate, and is treated with folic acid. **Always exclude B12 deficiency before giving folic acid alone**, because folate can correct the anaemia while the neurological damage progresses.

blocks.title: Folic acid alone can hide B12 deficiency
blocks.text: Folic acid may partly correct the blood count in B12 deficiency while subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord continues. Check B12 first, or replace both.

rows: Urobilinogen up; haemoglobinuria in intravascular lysis
blocks.caption: Laboratory pattern of haemolysis.

items: Haemolysis can be inherited (hereditary spherocytosis, G6PD deficiency, sickle cell disease, thalassaemia) or acquired (autoimmune with a positive direct antiglobulin test, mechanical valves, microangiopathy, infections such as malaria).
Sickle cell disease: a single substitution of valine for glutamic acid in the beta-globin chain produces HbS, which polymerises when deoxygenated and distorts red cells into sickles.
Sickle cells block small vessels (painful vaso-occlusive crises, acute chest syndrome, stroke, bone infarcts) and are destroyed early (chronic haemolysis, gallstones).
Management includes hydration, analgesia, oxygen if hypoxic, antibiotic prophylaxis and vaccination, folate, and hydroxycarbamide to raise fetal haemoglobin.
Thalassaemias are reduced production of globin chains (alpha or beta); trait is microcytic with normal iron stores, while major forms cause severe anaemia needing transfusion.

points: Classify anaemia by MCV, then use the film and iron studies to find the cause.
Iron deficiency: low ferritin, high TIBC, low saturation; look for a source of loss.
B12 deficiency causes macrocytosis and neurological damage; treat with intramuscular hydroxocobalamin and never give folic acid alone first.
Haemolysis shows raised reticulocytes, bilirubin and LDH with low haptoglobin.
Sickle cell disease is a haemoglobinopathy from HbS polymerisation causing vaso-occlusion and haemolysis; thalassaemia is reduced globin chain production.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman with heavy menstrual bleeding has Hb 88 g/L, MCV 66 fL, ferritin 5 micrograms/L and a raised TIBC. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: microcytosis, low ferritin and high TIBC with chronic blood loss.
distractorRationale.b: Anaemia of chronic disease has normal or high ferritin and low TIBC.
distractorRationale.d: Haemolysis is usually normocytic with raised reticulocytes.

questions.explanation: A low ferritin is the most specific marker of absent iron stores, and a high TIBC shows the body upregulating transferrin. Heavy menstrual loss is the commonest cause in premenopausal women.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis and a raised CRP has Hb 104 g/L, MCV 78 fL, ferritin 420 micrograms/L, low serum iron and low TIBC. What is the most likely cause of the anaemia?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: inflammation, high ferritin and low TIBC.
distractorRationale.b: Absolute iron deficiency would give a low ferritin and high TIBC.
distractorRationale.c: Thalassaemia trait gives a high red cell count and normal iron studies.

questions.explanation: Inflammation raises hepcidin, which locks iron in stores and reduces its availability to marrow, so serum iron is low while ferritin (an acute phase protein) is high. TIBC is low or normal rather than raised.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old strict vegan has MCV 118 fL, reduced vibration sense in the feet and a low serum B12. What is the correct treatment?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: replaces B12 and protects the nervous system.
distractorRationale.b: Folic acid alone can worsen the neurological damage.
distractorRationale.c: There is no evidence of iron deficiency, and MCV is high.
distractorRationale.d: The problem is a nutrient deficiency, not lack of erythropoietin.

questions.explanation: Macrocytosis with sensory neuropathy and low B12 in a vegan indicates dietary B12 deficiency. Replacement with hydroxocobalamin corrects the blood and halts the neurological damage, whereas folate alone would not.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman is jaundiced and pale. Hb 72 g/L, reticulocytes 14%, unconjugated bilirubin raised, haptoglobin undetectable, LDH raised, and the direct antiglobulin test is positive. What is the most likely diagnosis?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: haemolysis with a positive direct antiglobulin test.
distractorRationale.b: Aplastic anaemia has a low reticulocyte count.
distractorRationale.c: Iron deficiency has low reticulocytes and normal bilirubin and LDH.
distractorRationale.d: Pernicious anaemia is macrocytic and not primarily haemolytic.

questions.explanation: Raised reticulocytes, bilirubin and LDH with low haptoglobin show red cells are being destroyed faster than they are made. A positive direct antiglobulin test proves an antibody or complement coat on the cells, identifying autoimmune haemolysis.

questions.stem: Which molecular change underlies sickle cell disease?

options.text: Substitution of valine for glutamic acid in the beta-globin chain

questions.correctOptionText: Substitution of valine for glutamic acid in the beta-globin chain

distractorRationale.c: G6PD deficiency is a separate cause of haemolysis.
distractorRationale.d: Absent intrinsic factor causes pernicious anaemia.

questions.explanation: A single point mutation replaces glutamic acid with valine at position 6 of the beta chain. Deoxygenated HbS polymerises and distorts red cells, which then block small vessels and haemolyse early.

questions.stem: A patient has MCV 66 fL and a red cell count of 5.5 x 10^12/L. Calculate the Mentzer index (MCV divided by red cell count; a value below about 13 favours thalassaemia trait over iron deficiency). Give the unitless index.
questions.explanation: The index is 66 / 5.5 = 12.0, which is below 13. Together with a high red cell count and normal iron studies this favours thalassaemia trait rather than iron deficiency.

questions.stem: A man has serum iron 5 micromol/L and total iron-binding capacity 62 micromol/L. Calculate the transferrin saturation as a percentage.
questions.explanation: Transferrin saturation is serum iron divided by TIBC, times 100: 5 / 62 x 100 = 8.1%. This is low, consistent with iron deficiency, and would be accompanied by a low ferritin.

questions.stem: Describe the common causes of iron deficiency anaemia, how it is confirmed, and its management.
markingGuide: Causes: blood loss (menstrual, gastrointestinal), poor intake, malabsorption such as coeliac disease, increased demand in pregnancy
Confirmation: microcytic hypochromic picture, low ferritin, high TIBC, low transferrin saturation
Investigate the gastrointestinal tract in men and postmenopausal women
Oral iron replacement as first line, with intravenous iron if intolerant or malabsorbing
questions.explanation: Iron deficiency is a state of depleted stores, so management has two parts: replace the iron and, more importantly, remove the cause of loss or poor absorption. In men and postmenopausal women gastrointestinal blood loss from malignancy must be excluded.

questions.stem: A 20-year-old with sickle cell disease presents with severe bone pain. Explain the pathophysiology of the crisis, and list the laboratory features of the chronic haemolysis that accompanies the disease.
markingGuide: HbS results from valine substituted for glutamic acid in the beta chain
Deoxygenation, dehydration, infection or cold promote HbS polymerisation and sickling
Sickled cells obstruct small vessels causing ischaemia and pain
Raised unconjugated bilirubin and LDH, low haptoglobin
Mention of management: hydration, analgesia, oxygen if hypoxic
questions.explanation: Under stress HbS polymerises and rigid sickled cells occlude small vessels, causing tissue ischaemia and the pain of a vaso-occlusive crisis. The abnormal cells also survive only days, so there is permanent haemolysis with the standard laboratory markers.

questions.stem: True or false: giving folic acid alone to a patient with undiagnosed vitamin B12 deficiency is safe because it corrects the anaemia.
questions.explanation: Folic acid can partly correct the blood count while the neurological damage from B12 deficiency progresses. B12 status must be checked first, or both vitamins replaced.
